segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Let your eyes remain open or softly lowered. Feel the surface beneath you. This practice uses ordinary sensory details as coordinates back to the present room.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin by finding five things you can see. Let the eyes move slowly. Notice colour, shape, shadow, and small details without needing to name everything aloud.
[soft, slow, warm voice] One... Two... Three... Four... Five... Imagine each object lighting a tiny point on a map that says: you are here.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Now notice four things you can physically feel. Clothing on skin... feet on the floor... air on the face... the weight of your hands.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let each contact be simple evidence of the present. Four quiet coordinates transmitted from the body to the little control room of attention.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Listen for three sounds. Perhaps one is distant, one is near, and one is so ordinary that the mind had edited it out.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice two scents, or simply two qualities of the air. If scent is faint, you might notice coolness and warmth instead. There is no need to force a result.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice one taste, even if it is neutral. Let this final coordinate be small and unremarkable. The ordinary world is allowed to be enough.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] Feel all five senses sharing the same room. Thoughts may still be loud, but they are no longer the only signal on the map.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Choose one steady contact point, perhaps both feet or the back of the body. Rest attention there for several easy breaths.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Look around once more and notice where you are, what time of day it seems to be, and one next action that can be taken gently.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Keep the coordinates with you: seeing, touching, hearing, air, and taste. Move when ready, one ordinary step at a time.
